about: How customers of three Tennessee shops type into a website chat and into Telegram. Lower case where a thumb leaves it, apostrophes dropped, autocorrect left in (breaks for brakes, tired for tires), y'all and yall both. Every opening carries its voice and the channels it fits; a Telegram opening may name the advisor, a web opening never knows one.

voices.says: lower-case fragments, no punctuation, one line
dictated or typed in one breath, run-on, no full stops, a voice-to-text word gone wrong
polite and complete: a greeting, a full sentence, thank you
short, an emoji doing the work of a sentence
a desk, a keyboard, full sentences, unit numbers, wants it itemized
older and formal, signs the message, explains more than asked
a photo first, two or three words after
one word or two, the rest is the reader's problem
